description: Cilium's version pin lives in THIS repo, not gitops, because Cilium is
deliberately not an ArgoCD Application — ArgoCD cannot install the network
it needs in order to run, so k3s's HelmChart controller owns it (see
docs/runbooks/cilium-adoption.md). That closed the ownership gap and left
an upgrade-path gap: Renovate's `argocd` manager reads chart pins out of
ArgoCD Application manifests, and there is no such manifest to read.
So Renovate is pointed at this repo too. It still RUNS from the gitops
repository's CI (a manually dispatched workflow), because this repo has no
CI of its own, and standing up a runner here to bump one line would be a new
moving part bought for nothing. RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES lists both repos.
DELIBERATELY NARROW. The private repo holds ~40 docker-compose files with pinned
image tags. An unscoped Renovate would open dozens of PRs against services
that have no test, no staging and no rollback story, on a repo with no CI to
validate any of it — noise that would get the whole thing muted within a
week. enabledManagers is therefore the custom manager ONLY. Widening this is
a deliberate decision that should come with somewhere for those PRs to be
MANAGERS: Only the regex manager below. Nothing else in this repo is under Renovate's control.

customManagers.description: roles/cilium/defaults/main.yml: cilium_version: "1.17.5". This is the pin the HelmChart manifest renders, so bumping it here and running the role is the entire upgrade — helm-controller performs a `helm upgrade` on the adopted release.

packageRules.description: Never grouped, never automerged, and the PR body says what the reviewer is actually deciding. This is the CNI: a bad bump takes pod networking for the whole cluster, and the failure is quiet — existing pods keep working while new ones cannot schedule. One minor per PR (separateMultipleMinor, approved 2026-09-25): Cilium supports upgrades only minor-to-next-minor, and the default proposed 1.17->1.20 in one step (#4, closed) — each minor runs through the ansible role on its own.
prBodyNotes: :warning: **This is the CNI.** Nothing in CI proves a Cilium bump works — this repo has no CI, and rendering is not running.

Before merging: read the upstream upgrade notes for CRD and datapath changes, then **test on `preprod-1` first** (`cilium_manage` is already true there). The adoption runbook's phase-2 method applies unchanged — record daemonset generation, pod identity and `cilium-config` before and after, and keep a real traffic probe running across it.

Merging this PR changes nothing on its own. The upgrade happens when the `cilium` role next runs and k3s's helm-controller performs the `helm upgrade`. Unlike a chart bump in gitops, there is no ArgoCD to apply it for you.

packageRules.description: A Cilium major is a datapath migration, not a version bump. Dashboard approval means it cannot even open as a PR without a human asking for it.
